title: Sentry MCP
snippet:
# Sentry MCP Server
Connects AI assistants to Sentry for searching errors, analyzing performance, triaging issues, reading documentation, and managing projects — all via the Model Context Protocol.
All connections use OAuth. The first connection will trigger an authentication flow to connect to your Sentry account.
## Connecting
The base MCP server address is: `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`
You can optionally scope the connection to an organization or project:
- `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}` — scoped to one organization
- `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug}` — scoped to one project
When scoped, tools automatically default to the constrained org/project and unnecessary discovery tools are hidden. Scoping to a project is recommended when possible.
### Query Parameters
- `?experimental=1` — Enable forward-looking tool variants and experimental features
Parameters can be combined: `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/my-org/my-project?experimental=1`
## Setup Instructions
### Claude Code
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug}
```
### Cursor
Use the "Install MCP Server" button, or manually add to MCP settings:
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"sentry": {
"url": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug}"
}
}
}
```
### VSCode
Command Palette → "MCP: Add Server" → HTTP → enter the endpoint:
```
https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug}
```
### Other Clients
Any MCP-compatible client can connect using the HTTP transport at the endpoint URL above.
## Local Server via the Sentry CLI
Install the Sentry CLI and log in, then register `sentry mcp` as a stdio MCP server. It uses the CLI login, so the MCP config needs no token.
```bash
curl https://cli.sentry.dev/install -fsS | bash
sentry auth login
claude mcp add sentry -- sentry mcp
```
Other clients take the same command:
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"sentry": {
"command": "sentry",
"args": ["mcp"]
}
}
}
```
The CLI also installs with `brew install getsentry/tools/sentry`, `npm install -g sentry`, or `irm https://cli.sentry.dev/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows. See https://cli.sentry.dev/getting-started/.
Pass a target after the command to limit it:
- `sentry mcp my-org/` — Limit to one organization
- `sentry mcp my-org/my-project` — Limit to a specific project

# mcp
Start a local Sentry MCP server
## Usage
Section titled “Usage”
### `sentry mcp [<org/project>]`
Section titled “sentry mcp [<org/project>]”
Start a local Sentry MCP server
**Arguments:**
| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `[<org/project>]` | <org>/ (an organization) or <org>/<project> to limit calls to |
**Options:**
| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--access-token <access-token>` | Deprecated: set SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN instead |
| `--org <org>` | Limit every call to this organization |
| `--project <project>` | Limit calls to this project |
| `--skills <skills>` | Skills to grant, comma-separated (default: active skills; seer is left out on self-hosted) |
| `--all-skills` | Grant every active skill, including seer on self-hosted |
| `--disable-skills <disable-skills>` | Skills to remove, comma-separated |
| `--experimental` | Enable forward-looking tool variants and experimental features |
| `--agent-provider <agent-provider>` | LLM provider for AI-powered search: openai, azure-openai, anthropic, or openrouter |
| `--openai-base-url <openai-base-url>` | OpenAI API base URL |
| `--openai-model <openai-model>` | OpenAI model (default: gpt-5) |
| `--anthropic-base-url <anthropic-base-url>` | Anthropic API base URL |
| `--anthropic-model <anthropic-model>` | Anthropic model (default: claude-sonnet-4-5) |
| `--mcp-url <mcp-url>` | MCP server URL reported in telemetry |
**Examples:**
```
# Start the server with the current CLI loginsentry mcp
# Limit every call to one organizationsentry mcp acme/
# Limit calls to one projectsentry mcp acme/web
# Grant every skill, including seer on self-hostedsentry mcp --all-skills
# Grant only some skillssentry mcp --skills inspect,triage
# Pick the LLM provider for AI-powered searchsentry mcp --agent-provider anthropic
```
All commands support `--json` for machine-readable output and `--fields` to select specific JSON fields.
`sentry mcp` starts the local stdio Sentry MCP server using the active Sentry CLI session. Authenticate once with `sentry auth login`; no separate MCP login or token cache is required.

Section titled “Configure an MCP client”
Point your MCP client at the installed Sentry CLI:
```

```

title: docs.sentry.io/product/snapshots/agentic-workflow
snippet:
Connect an AI coding assistant to Sentry's MCP server so it can pull snapshot diffs, images, and baselines on your behalf. This lets you investigate snapshot failures by asking the agent, instead of clicking through the Sentry UI or downloading images by hand. It complements the [local CLI workflow](https://docs.sentry.io/product/snapshots/local-testing.md): MCP is built for agent-assisted investigation and review, while `sentry-cli` is built for local downloads and diffing.

Sentry's [MCP server](https://mcp.sentry.dev) connects your AI assistant to Sentry over the Model Context Protocol. Follow the setup and authentication instructions there for your client (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, and others).
The Sentry MCP has been optimized to retrieve Snapshot results for agentic workflows. If you'd like, you can also fetch the data via the [REST API](https://docs.sentry.io/api/snapshots.md) and expose scripts to agents.
Connect using one of these endpoints:
* `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`: base endpoint
* `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}`: scoped to one organization
* `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug}`: scoped to one project (recommended)
The first connection starts an OAuth flow to link your Sentry account.

To go further, grant the agent the advanced snapshot tools by enabling the **Preprod Snapshots** capability on the MCP authorization screen (it's off by default; check it when you first connect, or re-authorize to add it later). These tools let the agent fetch full-resolution images, list unchanged images, and look up an app's latest baseline. They give the agent more options but take up more of its context window while enabled.

title: GitHub - getsentry/toolkit: Agentic tooling for Sentry
snippet:
This repository contains the Sentry CLI, the Sentry MCP server, and shared packages. For the CLI, see the [CLI guide](/getsentry/toolkit/blob/main/docs/cli/README.md) and the published documentation at [https://cli.sentry.dev/](https://cli.sentry.dev/).

Sentry's MCP service is primarily designed for human-in-the-loop coding agents. Our tool selection and priorities are focused on developer workflows and debugging use cases, rather than providing a general-purpose MCP server for all Sentry functionality.
This remote MCP server acts as middleware to the upstream Sentry API, optimized for coding assistants like Cursor, Claude Code, and similar development tools. It's based on [Cloudflare's work towards remote MCPs](https://blog.cloudflare.com/remote-model-context-protocol-servers-mcp/).
## Getting Started
You'll find everything you need to know by visiting the deployed service in production:
[https://mcp.sentry.dev](https://mcp.sentry.dev)
If you're looking to contribute, learn how it works, or to run this for self-hosted Sentry, continue below.
### Claude Code Plugin
Install as a Claude Code plugin for automatic subagent delegation:
```
claude plugin marketplace add getsentry/sentry-mcp
claude plugin install sentry-mcp@sentry-mcp
```
This provides a `sentry-mcp` subagent that Claude automatically delegates to when you ask about Sentry errors, issues, traces, or performance.
For forward-looking tool variants and features:
```
claude plugin install sentry-mcp@sentry-mcp-experimental
```
### Stdio vs Remote
While this repository is focused on acting as an MCP service, we also support a `stdio` transport. This is still a work in progress, but is the easiest way to adapt run the MCP against a self-hosted Sentry install.
**Note:** The AI-powered search tools (`search_errors`, `search_traces`, `search_logs`, `search_issues`, etc.) require an LLM provider (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, or OpenRouter). These tools use natural language processing to translate queries into Sentry's query syntax. Without a configured provider, these specific tools will be unavailable, but all other tools will function normally.
To utilize the `stdio` transport, you'll need to create an User Auth Token in Sentry with the necessary scopes. As of writing this is:
```
org:read
project:read
project:write
team:read
team:write
event:write
```
Launch the transport:
```
npx @sentry/mcp-server@latest --access-token=sentry-user-token
```

snippet:
Install and authenticate the Sentry MCP server
The Sentry MCP server is a cloud-hosted service with no package to maintain. Run the command below in your terminal to register it with Claude Code, then launch Claude Code with `claude`. When prompted, sign in with your Sentry account and grant the requested permissions.
[ Sentry MCP server documentation ](https://mcp.sentry.dev/)
`Add Sentry MCP to Claude Code`
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp
```

With Sentry's MCP server connected to Claude Code, your AI agent can search through errors, traces, and logs to pinpoint root causes and ship the fix in a fraction of the time it would take manually.
- Installed and authenticated the Sentry MCP server in Claude Code
- Asked Claude to list and summarize open issues from your Sentry project
- Had Claude pull full error context: stack traces, structured logs, and related spans
- Applied a bug fix directly inside your editor with Claude's help
